document_check.note: Document is Ahn J, Kim M, 'Effects of exercise therapy on global cognitive function and, depression in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis', Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics 106 (2023) 104855. It pools RCTs of exercise in MCI; pooled SMD 0.65 (0.39 to 0.91) for global cognition matches the cited result.

cited_result: Pooled standardised mean difference 0.65 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.91) for global cognitive function, exercise versus control, in older adults with MCI: 21 RCTs, 1,916 analysed, random effects, I² 85%, outcomes at end of intervention.
tool_reason: The cited result is a pooled estimate from a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials.

domains.rationale: The review is registered and has an appropriate PICO. However, eligibility is restricted to studies from 2010 onwards without justification, and language or publication-status restrictions are not reported.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: This review was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Review (PROSPERO: CRD42022325449).

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: participants: older adults aged 60 years and more who met the diagnostic criteria for MCI (Petersen et al., 1999, 2014); interventions: aerobic, resistance, multicomponent, and neuromotor exercises; comparisons: no treatment, usual care, health education, and stretching; outcomes: the primary outcome was global cognitive function, and the secondary outcome was depression; timing of outcome measurement: end of exercise therapy; study design: only RCTs.

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: those with insufficient statistics (means, standard deviations, and sample sizes were not reported: t and F values were not presented) were excluded: those with very low baseline levels of depression were also excluded

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: We searched international, and domestic databases from January 1, 2010, to May 31, 2022

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched methods sections 2.1 and 2.2 for language restriction, publication status or unpublished data; none stated

domains.domain: Domain 2: Identification and selection of studies
domains.rationale: The database range is broad. However, the reported strategy searches title/abstract only, applies an RCT publication-type filter and an unexplained 2010 start date, and gives inconsistent end dates (2020, 2021 and 2022). Independent duplicate screening is not stated.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources?
signalling.quote: We searched nine international databases (PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, SPORTDiscus, Web of Science, and ProQuest global) as well as six domestic databases (RISS, NDSL, KMbase, KISS, KISTI, and NAL).

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used?
signalling.quote: Moreover, searches in Google Scholar and manual searches of reference lists were conducted simultaneously.

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: Filters: Human, Randomized Controlled Trial, from 2010/1/1-2020/5/31

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: The search period was from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2021, and the final search was performed until May 31, 2022.

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: Searched section 2.3 for independent duplicate screening; only searching is described as independent: 'Two researchers searched the databases independently and used Endnote X7 (Microsoft Corp., Redmond, WA, USA) to remove duplicate studies. The titles/abstracts were reviewed according to the eligibility criteria'

domains.domain: Domain 3: Data collection and study appraisal
domains.rationale: RoB 2 was applied in duplicate and study characteristics are tabulated. However, duplicate data extraction is not reported. It is also unclear whether post-intervention values or change scores were used, or how instruments scored in opposite directions (ADAS-Cog vs MMSE/MoCA) were harmonised, and studies lacking statistics were excluded rather than authors contacted.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: Searched section 2.3 for duplicate or independent extraction; only 'We extracted the study information, characteristics of the participants, and exercise therapy characteristics' is given

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: The characteristics of the 22 articles that were included in this meta-analysis are presented in Table 1.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Pre-, post-, mean, standard deviation, and number of samples were mainly used in the data, and if only the statistics of the confidence interval were presented, the standard deviation was calculated according to the formula (Wan et al., 2014).

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: The risk of bias in the selected studies was assessed using Cochrane’s risk of bias tool 2.0 (Higgins & Cochrane, 2020), as revised in 2019.

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: After two researchers independently evaluated five areas (randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, outcome measurement, and selection of the reported result)

domains.rationale: Several problems affect the synthesis. It pools heterogeneous instruments and comparators, includes a crossover trial with no stated handling, and appears to include two reports of one trial (Lam 2011 and 2012 share randomised numbers 171:218). Heterogeneity is very high (I² 85%) with no prediction interval, and subgroup conclusions rest on within-subgroup significance although the between-type test is null (p=0.69). Risk of bias is not used in the synthesis. The leave-one-out analysis reports a baseline of 0.53, inconsistent with the 0.65 pooled estimate.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: Of the 22 included studies, 21 RCTs were analyzed to investigate the effect of exercise therapy on global cognitive function.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: Searched methods and results for the analyses pre-specified in the PROSPERO record; moderator analyses are presented as a response to heterogeneity: 'Therefore, moderator analysis was performed.'

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity of research questions, designs and outcomes?
signalling.quote: Lam et al. (2011) Hong Kong RCT, triple blind R=171:218; A=135:194 ... Lam et al. (2012) Hong Kong RCT, single blind R=171:218; A=92:169 ... Phoemsapthawee et al. (2016) Thailand RCT, cross over

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: the heterogeneity was high (I2 = 85%, τ2 = 0.2752, chi-square = 129.15, p < 0.001). Therefore, moderator analysis was performed.

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: The mean effects adjusted by omitting these studies one by one showed a slight difference from the mean effect size of 0.53 in all studies; however, there was no statistically significant difference.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Analysis of the risk of bias assessment of the 22 included RCTs showed that 11 (50%) were “low risk,” 11 (50%) were of “some concerns,” and 0 (0%) was “high risk.”

domains.domain: Phase 3: Risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The limitations section does not address the search restrictions, heterogeneity or primary-study bias, and treats a non-significant Egger test as proof of no publication bias. Conclusions emphasise within-subgroup statistical significance.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
signalling.quote: Third, although no publication bias was present as all possible studies were included, experimental studies of gray literature and ongoing trials could not be identified.

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: This review systematically classified various types of exercise therapy in older adults with MCI according to the ACSM (Riebe et al., 2018).

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: Aerobic and resistance exercises were effective in improving global cognitive function, Whereas multicomponent and neuromotor exercises were not.

overall: High risk of bias (ROBIS: domains 1, 2 and 4 high, domain 3 unclear; phase 3 high)
overall_rationale: The search is restricted by date, field and publication-type filter, with inconsistent dates, and the eligibility date cut-off is unjustified. The synthesis pools heterogeneous measures (I² 85%), appears to double-count one trial, ignores primary-study risk of bias and over-interprets subgroups. The interpretation does not address these concerns, so the review is at high risk of bias for the pooled SMD of 0.65.

applicability.domain: Relevance of review question to the cited use
applicability.rationale: The review question (exercise vs no exercise or attention control in adults aged 60 or over with Petersen-defined MCI, global cognition at end of intervention) matches the cited use as a short-programme effect in already-diagnosed MCI.
